title.narrative: Operationalising the (MOU 2022 – 2027)/UN-HABITAT Country Programme Document (HCPD 2023 – 2027) for Nigeria

description.narrative: 1. NIGERIA: COUNTRY OVERVIEW Nigeria, with a total population estimated at 206 million by the end of 2020, is the largest country in sub-Saharan Africa, both in terms of size of the economy and population. According to the Common Country Analysis of the United Nations (2021), Nigeria’s current population growth rate of 2.59 percent a year ranks Nigeria as “the fastest growing population of any country with at least 100 million people.” This population comprises a large proportion of young people aged 0 – 14 years who make up 43.2% of the population, with 63% of the population aged 24 years old or younger and females making up an estimated 49.3% of the population. Overall, the demographics of Nigeria show that roughly 81% of the population are either female, youth, or children . Based on current trends, it is estimated that Nigeria could attain a population of up to 401 million by 2050, making it the third most populous country in the world. 2. NATIONAL URBANISATION CONTEXT Nigeria’s rapid population growth has been characterised by an even higher urban population growth rate which, at at 4.1% per year, has seen its urban populations growing almost twice as fast as the national growth. Rising from 9.4% in 1950 to 52% in 2020, the share of the population living in cities is expected to rise to 70% by 2050 when it is predicted that the country will be the third most populous country in the world with a total population of over 400 million. This large urban population is distributed among several fast growing cities in the six geo-political zones of the country as the number of cities with populations of 20,000 and above rose from 56 in 1953 to 183 in 1963 and 359 in 1991. Currently, eight cities are estimated to have populations of more than a million people, 81 cities with between 100,000 and one million people, and 248 cities with between 10,000 and 100,000 people. The urban transformation in Nigeria has been accompanied by some critical challenges. These include the rapid growth in the proportion of urban residents who live in slum conditions (estimated at about 58.8% ), a rising housing deficit estimated at between 16-18 million units; insecure land tenure, poor and inadequate infrastructure and lack of basic urban services. Though the country’s urban slum population currently estimated as 53.3 percent has witnessed a decline of 20 percentage points since 1990, there has been growth in the absolute slum population, rising from 21.8 million in 1990 to 57.7 million in 2018 . 3. STRATEGIC FOCUS OF UN-HABITAT COUNTRY PROGRAMME (2023 - 2027) The strategic focus of the HCPD, articulated following a comprehensive stakeholder engagement and in line with Federal Government of Nigeria priorities, is to promote sustainable urbanisation through the development of inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable cities and communities as transformative forces for achieving economic growth, peace and improved living conditions for all in Nigeria in line with the SDGs. The HCPD will facilitate sustainable urban development in Nigeria through implementation of identified strategic interventions within the context of national and global development priorities, notably Nigeria’s National development Plan, the Africa Union’s Agenda 2063, the United Nations 2030 Agenda and its Post-2015 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in particular Goal 11, of “Making cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable” as well as the New Urban Agenda, implemented within the context of the UNSDCF 2023 - 2027. The HCPD is founded on six Pillars, comprising an overarching strategic focus on ‘Achieving Sustainable Urbanisation,’ three Thematic Pillars and two Cross-cutting Pillars which translate into Four Programming Outcome Areas for the HCPD as follows: a) OVERARCHING PILLAR: Achieving Sustainable Urbanisation: OUTCOME 1: Reduced Spatial Inequality and Poverty in Communities Across the Urban-Rural Continuum. FOCUS AREAS: National/State Urban Policies; Rural/Urban Linkages; Strategic Spatial/territorial Planning b) THEMATIC PILLAR 1: Poverty Reduction and Social Inclusion/Transformative actions for local economic development OUTCOME 2: Increased and Equal Access to Basic Services, Sustainable Mobility and Public Space. FOCUS AREAS: Improved access to land, secure tenure, and affordable housing; Participatory Urban Renewal/Slum Upgrading; Improved livelihoods and skills; Empowerment of youth, women and vulnerable groups c) THEMATIC PILLAR 2: Implementation of Resilience and Durable Solutions in Human Settlements OUTCOME 3: Enhanced Resilience of Communities, the Built Environment and Infrastructure to impacts of climate change, disasters and forced migration.
